content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term (1-3 days) after sentiment spikes (sentiment > 0.3), especially when forecast shows sharp upward moves.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.2) — model tends to ignore downward momentum.
- Overshoot in the 7-14 day horizon after a spike — model overreacts to recent highs, then corrects too late.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in the 15-30 day horizon, especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- Lagged correction: true prices often dip 1-2 days after model peaks — model fails to anticipate short-term reversal.
- Sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment is rising, model overweights it; when sentiment is falling, model underweights it — adjust forecast by 5-10% downward if sentiment drops below 0.2.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high — reduce by 1-2% for each 0.10 drop in sentiment over last 5 days.
